title: File:Theban region, Deir el-Medina, TT1, tomb of Sennedjem, 1905-1914, photo 5 of 9 - Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin C00132.jpg
credit: Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin - online catalogue
desc: North wall (back) from the tomb of Sennedjem (TT 1). The god Anubis is performing the embalming ritual on the mummy of the deceased. Around him is the text from Spell 1 of the Book of the Dead. On the right, the god Osiris inside a shrine.
name: sennedjem_anubis

title: File:Theban region, Deir el-Medina, TT1, tomb of Sennedjem, 1905-1914, photo 3 of 9 - Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin C00131.jpg
credit: Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin - online catalogue
desc: North wall (back) from the tomb of Sennedjem (TT 1). On the right, the god Anubis leads the deceased by the hand. The text accompanying the scene describes Anubis’ guidance of the deceased in front of the gods of the Duat. In the centre, Sennedjem is kneeling in front of a pile of offerings in honour of the god Osiris (who is on the left but not visible in this photograph).
name: sennedjem_osiris

title: File:Theban region, Deir el-Medina, TT1, tomb of Sennedjem, 1905-1914, photo 2 of 9 - Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin C00134.jpg
credit: Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin - online catalogue
desc: South wall, west side (left) of the entrance to the tomb of Sennedjem (TT 1). In the upper register, the deceased is resting on a small bed between the goddesses Isis (left) and Nephthys (right) in the form of falcons. The register below displays some relatives, including his son Bunakhtef, dressed as a sem-priest wearing a leopard skin and presenting a libation to the deceased couple, Sennedjem a
name: sennedjem_ba

title: File:Theban region, Deir el-Medina, TT1, tomb of Sennedjem, 1905-1914, photo 1 of 9 - Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin C00135.jpg
credit: Archivio fotografico Museo Egizio, Turin - online catalogue
desc: West wall (left) from the tomb of Sennedjem (TT 1). Above, two jackals seated on a shrines; the lower register shows the deceased Sennedjem together with his wife Iyneferti as they worship the gods of the Duat, including Osiris (the first in the top row from the left) and Ra-Horakhty (the first in the bottom row from the left).
name: sennedjem_hall

title: File:Great Hymn to the Aten from Ay’s EA25 tomb.jpg
author: Tobeytravels
desc:
This is an excellent view of Akhenaten's Great Hymn to the Aten at the Right side doorway of Ay's EA25 South Tomb at Amarna.  Ay's tomb is notable for featuring the longest and most detailed surviving copy of the Great Hymn to the Aten, written to the sun-disk deity Aten out of all the Amarna tombs. 
Ay, who later became pharaoh himself and succeeded Akhenaten's son Tutankhamun to the throne built
